parameterBindings.derivation: the comp's actual announced target time — GS's durTargetTime 600 (competition.json familyRows.Dur), the value the club actually ran. Equals the seed's declared default, but is bound explicitly (BeforeFlying, competition-wide) per the story: the binding records the club's announced value, never leans on the seed author's default.

the largest ACTUAL group size in the realised draw (the fixture draws one group of ten per round, R1-R3/G1). The seed declares no default — the value must be bound before /prescribe-draw (CompetitionSetup parameters freeze once the draw is accepted).
the rounds actually flown (the fixture's three distinct RoundNos), matching the phase validity the seed resolves at finalisation. No default — bound before /prescribe-draw.

the fixture has NO re-flights (every scores-raw row carries OriginalRoundNo == RoundNo and ReFlightNo == 0), so no data determines the value and it is never exercised. NZ.3.12.5 l states no minimum for a re-flight group (entitlement only: 'hindered or aborted by an unexpected event not within his control'), so 1 is the least-constraining rulebook-consistent choice — the engine's own members-empty refusal is the real floor. Not an assertion about this club's practice.

metricMappings.mechanism: seed-declared whenNotRecorded (Flag true), resolved by the engine (FlightMetricResolution tier 1, metric-absence-semantics.md) — the harness emits NO assumed values; the capture map stays exactly the parity replay's and records only what the fixture data carries.
metricMappings.justification: P1 (assumed-clean unless recorded to the contrary): the club records exceptions, not compliance — a clean flight is recorded as just time and distance. NZ.2.4.6 cancels the flight and scores zero when the nose does not come to rest within 75 m of the centre of the designated landing spot; an unrecorded cancellation is the negative recording of the exception. Corroborated inside the foil's own data: every scores-raw row carries LandingOver75m false (no contrary record). The seed declares the flag as the flightValidWhen gate, matching NZ.2.4.6's shape — it zeroes the flight, not the bonus.

metricMappings.mechanism: seed-declared whenNotRecorded (Flag false), resolved by the engine — no harness-emitted values.
metricMappings.justification: P1: NZ.3.12.2 d removes the landing points when the model sustains significant damage during the landing and, in the CD's opinion, is not safely flyable — an exception a timer/helper records. No GS column records it on this fixture, so the benign value (no such damage; the landing points stand per NZ.3.12.2 b) is the negative recording. The seed declares the flag inside the conditional gating its landing lookup (scoreNormalised).

metricMappings.mechanism: seed-declared whenNotRecorded (Flag false), resolved by the engine — no harness-emitted values.
metricMappings.justification: P1: NZ.3.12.2 e removes the landing points when the model touches the pilot or helper during the landing — an exception. No contrary record in the fixture data, so the benign value (no contact) stands.

notes: UNWITNESSED triaged candidate — landing-distance precision: the seed declares Ceiling 1 m per NZ.2.4.5 ('the measured distance is rounded to the next full metre') where GS truncates. Every recorded landing here is a whole metre (3.0/4.0/5.0), so the difference cannot appear on this data. A provenance note, NOT a ledger entry: a triaged difference that fails to appear FAILS the scenario (WI-2.3).

UNWITNESSED triaged candidate — normalise rounding: GS's proven grid rounds normalised cells HalfUp to 1 dp while the seed leaves the rulebook's values exact (the rule states no normalised-score rounding precision). Every normalised cell on this fixture is a whole number (440/835/1030 and zeros), so no fractional cell witnesses the difference. A provenance note, not a ledger entry.

UNWITNESSED triaged candidate — EqualPlaces tie-break: the seed declares an equalPlaces tie-break where the NZ rulebook states none (docs/rules/nz/00-nz-general-rules.md §6), and GS's ladder carries its own RawScore secondary key. The seven zero-score pilots tie identically on both sides ('=4' with EqualPlaces), so no tie-break decision was exercised. A provenance note, not a ledger entry.

UNWITNESSED triaged candidate — ZeroRound penalties: the seed declares launchOutsideBuzzerWindow (NZ.3.12.1 h) and landedOutsideFieldBounds (NZ.3.12.4 a) as ZeroRound infractions. The fixture records no Penalty rows and no such violations, so the penalty path never runs. A provenance note, not a ledger entry.

triagedDifferences.difference: Raw score-cell composition: GS's stored RawScore folds the landing points into the pre-normalisation raw (flight 120 s = 120 pts + 3 m landing = 40 pts, stored 160), while the NZ rulebook composition the seed-run produces keeps the pre-normalisation raw at flight points only (120) and adds the landing points after normalisation (final cell 440 = 400 + 40, identical on both sides). Witnessed: raw cell 1/1/1/0/13 is 160 in GS's oracle, 120 in the seed-run.
triagedDifferences.citation: Rulebook: NZ.3.12.1 e — 'Landing points will be added to the normalized flight score to determine the overall score'; NZ.3.12.3 d — 'The contestant's final score will be the sum of the pilot's normalized flight score and the landing score'. Local practice: the club's GS grid composes landing into its persisted RawScore pre-normalisation (resolve-gliderscore-scoring-arithmetic.md D1). Triage kind 1 — local variation: the club ran a variant of the rulebook; correct on both sides.
